judged_text: The connection setup now performs an unconditional token refresh - a fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma credential write - on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, where the previous code created the jsforce Connection lazily and refreshed only when an API call actually needed a new token. Every booking operation touching a Salesforce calendar now incurs a synchronous round-trip to Salesforce and a DB write, burns Salesforce token-endpoint rate limits, and fails outright whenever Salesforce's token endpoint hiccups even though the stored access token is still valid - converting a transient Salesforce outage into total Salesforce unavailability.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor path now unconditionally performs a token refresh (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token" ...)`) and then persists the result via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no check of the existing credential’s expiry/validity before doing this refresh+DB write, so every instantiation will incur an external round-trip and a DB write, and will fail if the token endpoint is unavailable even if the stored access token would still work. The finding’s comparison to the *previous* lazy behavior can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the new unconditional refresh behavior is directly shown.
